title: Endpoint distribution for restricted walks
statement: Let $A$ be a symmetric stochastic matrix on a nonempty finite state space, and let $B$ be a set of states. For every $k\in\mathbb N$ and state $j$, the sum of the probabilities of all walks of length $k$ whose states all lie in $B$ and whose final state is $j$ equals the $j$th coordinate of the vector obtained by starting with mass $1/n$ on each state in $B$ and applying the matrix that retains only rows indexed by $B$, at each of the $k$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: Each row of A sums to one
B is a subset of the state space
